title: Post-incident: fill eval gaps and add automated regression gates for config/model rollouts
creator: Luca Tran
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed a quality regression after a controlled rollout of a quantized model variant (q8_optimized) combined with a change to runtime batching policy (continuous_batching=true) and a caching flag (prefix_cache_enabled=false). Customer-facing signals showed increased semantic recall failures for long-context summarization prompts. The change was rolled back within 3 hours, but the incident revealed gaps in our eval and gating coverage that allowed the regression to reach production.

Root cause analysis:
- Our pre-rollout eval matrix tested quantized variants and batch policy in isolation but did not test the specific combination (quantization + continuous batching + prefix cache disabled) that surfaced the regression.
- Long-tail prompt formats (multi-paragraph legal/documents with structured bullets) are underrepresented in the presubmit eval corpus.
- The rollout pipeline lacked an automated quality gate that evaluates top-customer prompt families and combinatorial config permutations beyond single-dimension checks.
- Telemetry surfaced the regression late because our production-quality monitors are token-cost/latency focused and only a minority of production requests hit the semantic-recall probe sets.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- Rolled back the q8_optimized variant for the affected shard and re-enabled prefix caching default.
- Tagged and quarantined the failing rollout and blocked further deployments of q8_optimized without expanded testing.
- Created an ad-hoc eval job that replays customer-sanitized failing requests through candidate config matrix to confirm failure surface.

Follow-up scope (this ticket):
1) Expand eval coverage: add combinatorial matrix tests for model quantization x batching policy x cache flags. Include at least: {q4, q8, q8_optimized} x {continuous_batching on/off} x {prefix_cache on/off}.
2) Long-tail prompt augmentation: curate and sanitize additional prompt families from incident logs and partner customers (legal, transcripts, code-mixed). Add those to the primary regression probe set.
3) Automated gated rollout: implement a new gating step in the deployment pipeline that runs a fast, representative eval (top-100 probe families) and blocks rollout if per-probe BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-recall drops exceed thresholds.
4) Post-deploy smoke tests: run lightweight semantic probes against a production shadow stream for first 30 minutes and auto-rollback on failures above threshold.
5) Observability improvements: add a quality-regression dashboard with diffed metrics (per-probe delta, per-route failure rate), and an alert rule for sudden per-hour increases in probe failure rate.
6) Ownership and process: create an "eval-gap" tracker and add to the release checklist for model/config changes; require PM sign-off for any config that expands combinatorial state.

Deliverables and acceptance criteria:
- New combinatorial eval jobs added to CI (passes on baseline run) and scheduled nightly.
- New probe families (>=50 unique prompt templates) merged into the regression corpus with metadata for source, sanitizer, and owner.
- Deployment pipeline gating step implemented and validated on a canary release (test run ID: canary-2026-03-12-42).
- Dashboard and alerting in Console-Observability created and documented (link in attachments).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Expanding combinatorial testing increases CI runtime and compute costs; we'll prioritize fast approximations and probabilistic sampling for nightly runs and reserve full matrix runs for pre-release runs.
- Strict gating may slow down legitimate rollouts; thresholds must be tuned based on historical false-positive rates.

Estimated timeline: 3 sprints (approx 6 weeks) for phased rollout: quick wins (smoke tests, dashboard) in 1 sprint, combinatorial tests and corpus expansion in sprint 2, pipeline gating and process changes in sprint 3.

Notes: This ticket focuses on engineering deliverables. Separate follow-ups will handle customer comms and formal postmortem write-up (ENG-4794).
